questions.question: In a chemical reaction, what do we call the starting chemical substances that undergo the reaction?
options: Catalysts
Products
Reactants
Solvents

questions.question: What is the scientific term for the new substances that are formed as a result of a chemical reaction?
options: Reactants
Products
Mixtures
Elements

questions.question: When a chemical reaction occurs, how do the atoms in the products compare to the atoms in the reactants?
options: They contain completely new and different atoms.
They contain exactly the same atoms.
Some atoms are destroyed, and new ones are made.
They contain twice as many atoms.

questions.question: Which of the following describes John Dalton’s early model of an atom?
options: A ball of positive charge containing negative electrons
A small positive nucleus surrounded by orbiting electrons
A sphere that cannot be broken up
A cloud of waves containing particles

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the composition of a chemical element?
options: It is made up of only one type of atom.
It contains a mixture of different compounds.
It is made of two different types of metal.
It can easily be broken down into simpler elements.

questions.question: In a chemical formula, what do the small subscript numbers written next to chemical symbols represent?
options: The temperature required for the reaction
The state of matter of each substance
The number of each type of atom in the compound
The relative electrical charge of the atoms

questions.question: Water (H₂O) and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) are different compounds containing hydrogen and oxygen. What makes them different compounds?
options: They contain completely different elements.
One is a mixture and the other is a compound.
They contain the same elements, but in a different ratio.
They have the exact same chemical properties.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of hazard symbols on chemical containers?
options: To indicate how expensive a chemical is
To describe the potential dangers of the substances
To show the state of matter at room temperature
To identify who manufactured the chemical

questions.question: What are metalloids?
options: Elements that have only the properties of metals
Elements that have some properties of metals and some of non-metals
Man-made elements that do not occur in nature
Elements that are highly explosive when wet

questions.question: How do the properties of a compound compare to the properties of the individual elements that formed it?
options: They are always a simple mathematical average of the elements.
They must be identical to the properties of the metal element.
They can be completely different from each of the individual elements.
They are always the same as the gaseous element involved.

questions.question: Which non-metal is an exception to the rule because it is a good conductor of both electricity and heat?
options: Sulfur
Graphite
Oxygen
Helium

questions.question: Where on the periodic table are metals and non-metals typically located?
options: Metals on the right side, non-metals on the left side
Metals in the top row, non-metals in the bottom row
Metals in the middle columns, non-metals in the outer rows
Metals on the left side and in the middle, non-metals on the right side

questions.question: Which group of elements is monatomic (exists as single atoms) and is found in the far-right column of the periodic table?
options: Halogens
Alkali metals
Noble gases
Transition metals

questions.question: When naming a simple compound made of a metal and a non-metal, how does the name of the non-metal change to show bonding has occurred?
options: It ends with '-ate'
It ends with '-ide'
It ends with '-ite'
It ends with '-ic'

questions.question: If a compound consists of metal atoms chemically bonded to -SO₄, what is the group name for this compound?
options: Metal carbonate
Metal nitrate
Metal sulfate
Metal chloride
